title: Prefetch Impact Oracle and Minimal-Patch Runbook for KV Cache-Induced Output Drift
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an automated 'Prefetch Impact Oracle' that attributes output divergence to KV/prefix cache hits introduced by runtime/config/model changes, plus a minimal runbook to produce targeted patches or rollforward decisions. The goal is to give engineers deterministic, signal-rich evidence in CI and canaries so rollouts can be gated by measurable semantic drift attributable to cache reuse. Deliverables: a reproducible fingerprinting + replay harness, an attribution scoring model, CI gating thresholds, and a one-click minimal-patch runbook that attempts safe mitigations (prefetch disable, prefix-scope pin, conservative kernel path).
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint captures request context, model variant, prefix-kv signature, and relevant runtime flags and is stable across replays

Differential replays (with-cache vs without-cache) run deterministically for 10k representative prompts and produce a per-prompt regression score using both token-level diffs and semantic embedding distance

CI integration posts a summarized regression report with top 20 highest-confidence cache-attributed regressions to GitHub PRs and blocks runtime/config rollouts when regression-score > 0.03 on a safety-tier prompt set
Minimal-patch runbook produces a reproducible mitigant branch (config patch + test) and automates a canary re-run, with a documented rollback decision matrix
Telemetry that attributes regression likelihood to one of {quantization-profile, kernel-selection, batching-policy, prefetch-enabled} with at least 70% precision on historical incidents
test_plan: Assemble 10k prompt corpus stratified by persona, sequence-length, and hotness (observed hit rate bins)
Instrument runtime to log compact cache fingerprint per request (prefix-hash, kv-version, model-id, kernel-id, quantize-tag)
Replay harness runs every PR: baseline (cache off), candidate (cache on) using identical RNG seeds and patched deterministic kernels
Compute three metrics: token-edit-distance, BLEU-ish overlap, and sentence-embedding cosine delta (SBERT) and combine into composite regression-score
Run needle tests: binary-search change attribution by toggling single config flags across controlled runs
runbook: 1) Detect: CI regression report flags composite-score > threshold on safety set
2) Snapshot: persist request fingerprints and both response artifacts (cache-on, cache-off) to /artifacts/cache-oracle/YYYYMMDD/
3) Isolate: run targeted binary toggles for quantize/kernel/batching/prefetch to identify smallest delta-producing flag
4) Patch: if prefetch is root-cause, publish minimal config patch that disables prefix-prefetch for the implicated model family and open hotfix PR
5) Canary: run canary of patched config on 5% dedicated traffic with shadow logging; compare composite-score to baseline
6) Rollforward vs Rollback: if canary composite-score improves by >= 50% of regression magnitude, rollforward; else rollback and escalate to runtime-ops
7) Postmortem: add reproducer prompts to golden-responses dataset and tag regression fingerprint for future automated detection
implementation_notes: Store fingerprints as small protobuf lines in s3://redwood-cache-oracle/ for fast replay fanout
Use a single deterministic RNG seed layer inside model runtime during replay to eliminate nondeterminism unrelated to cache state
Leverage existing golden-response dataset infra (ENG-20601) for baseline reference and augment it with cache-conditioned examples
Plan to reuse evaluation infra from ENG-42109 for shadow/parallel runs and ENG-31456 for canary runbook integration

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Replay nondeterminism due to optimized kernels. Mitigation: enable a deterministic kernel path flag during replay and compare against kernel-selected runs.
Risk: False positives from semantically equivalent paraphrases. Mitigation: include embedding-based semantic threshold and a human-review sampling step before blocking a rollout.
Risk: Storage blowup for artifacts. Mitigation: retain raw artifacts for 30 days and keep compact fingerprints + summaries indefinitely.

Risk: Attribution ambiguity when multiple flags change in a deploy. Mitigation: enforce CI atomic-change policy for runtime flags during rollout and require single-flag rollout per canary for 72 hours
